annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, fixed-run first-order strengthening, operational mixed-precision restarted MGS-GMRES contract, and formal composition of Theorem 6.3

assumptions: The dimension is positive; A is nonsingular; b is nonzero; xExact solves A*xExact=b; and Ainv has both inverse actions, so kappa_F(A)=||Ainv||_F*||A||_F uses the actual inverse.
One fixed execution uses the same positive unit roundoffs uHigh and uLow at every restart; no separate uHigh <= uLow restriction is imposed because Theorem 6.3 does not print one.
At every restart, the computed residual and update satisfy the exact high-precision equations (6.19) and (6.20), including their componentwise error bounds.

Every correction exposes the fully stored low-precision MGS projection, update, and normalization operations for a positive restart-dependent key dimension k_i <= n, identifies the cast residual with its norm times the first Arnoldi basis vector, and records the Arnoldi product, columnwise augmented least-squares, and rounded correction-formation models.

Each low-precision operation error is tied to uLow, and witness forms of conditions (3.5)-(3.8), the coefficients in (3.12), and the correction-level estimates inherited from the earlier MGS-GMRES analysis are explicit; no global Theorem 4.1 recurrence is stored.

A nonnegative bivariate polynomial represents the paper's dimension-only c(n,k), and each contraction and floor evaluates it at the actual restart key dimension k_i rather than at an artificial uniform index.
Every Lambda_i=c(n,k_i)*uLow*kappa_F(A) is a nonnegative strict contraction. The exact-real standard model excludes underflow, overflow, NaNs, and infinities.

The target gives exact affine inequalities as a strengthening of the paper's first-order lesssim notation; it does not introduce a fixed-precision remainder certificate or a stationary 1/(1-Lambda) denominator.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p16_t3_mixed_precision_geometric_convergence {n : Nat} (run : P16FixedMixedPrecisionGMRESRun n) (hLambda : forall i, 0 <= p16FixedMixedContraction run i and p16FixedMixedContraction run i < 1) : (forall i, actualBackwardError_(i+1) <= Lambda_i*actualBackwardError_i + backwardFloor_i) and (forall i, actualForwardError_(i+1) <= Lambda_i*actualForwardError_i + forwardFloor_i)
formal_statement.plain_language: For one fixed-precision restarted MGS-GMRES execution, every actual normalized backward and relative forward error obeys the paper's restart-local low-precision contraction plus its corresponding high-precision attainable floor.

informal_proof: At each restart, use the high-precision residual and update equations to split the next actual backward and forward errors into the low-precision MGS correction defect and the high-precision roundoff contribution. Apply the correction-level estimates inherited from the earlier MGS-GMRES analysis and the normalized high-precision bounds, both evaluated with c(n,k_i), and add the inequalities.
informal_statement: Theorem 6.3's fixed-run first-order contraction for actual mixed-precision restarted MGS-GMRES errors, with Lambda_i=c(n,k_i)uLow*kappa_F(A), backward floor c(n,k_i)uHigh, and forward floor c(n,k_i)uHigh*kappa_F(A).

tier_rationale: The mounted condition-L library supplies only generic Euclidean and Frobenius norm facts useful in the residual and update decompositions. It contains no MGS-Arnoldi execution model, restart-dependent key-dimension framework, mixed-precision operation linkage, actual GMRES error definitions, or Theorem 6.3 composition theorem. Both conditions must establish the paper-specific actual-error split and combine the two precision regimes, so the selected result remains an extension task.
